verdicts.tldr: Once the scan budget runs out, a definition line with text after its URL is still deleted, so a fence inside that text escapes the trackers and the realm's footer renders inside a code block
verdicts.details: The merge gates the PR's own 'only whitespace may follow a definition' check on skipSpace's ok (`if ok && end < len(s) && s[end] != '\n'`). Once the budget runs out, the check is skipped and scanLRDTail returns true. The line `[a]: u ```` is then taken as a definition, `[a]: u` is deleted, and the ` ```` left at line start was never seen by closeFencesAtDedent. In the PR's pre-merge commit 1c377bf89 the whitespace skip was unbudgeted and the check always ran. The merge base has no check at all and deletes the line even within budget. So the merge reopened, for budget-exhausted inputs, the hole the PR's lrd-text-after-destination case claims to close. Fix: make the check fail closed, `if !ok || end < len(s) && s[end] != '\n' { return 0, false }`; TestEscapeBlockHazards and TestEscapeBlockHazardsRich stay green with that change.

verdicts.angle: reach (missed class member: container-relative fence indent)
verdicts.tldr: When a user's fence sits inside a list item, indented 4-6 spaces, the head leaves `[home]` in that item unescaped, and it links to the realm's own [home] definition; the merge base escaped it
verdicts.details: parseFenceOpener accepts at most 3 spaces of absolute indent, so a fence opened 4-6 spaces in inside a list item is invisible to the tracker. That is indent 0-3 from the item's content column, which CommonMark treats as a fence. The item's closer at the content column then reads to the tracker as an opener, and the item text after it is left unescaped. Under goldmark that text is a live paragraph inside the item, and `[home]` binds to the definition the realm chrome declares after the user text. The merge base escapes the same inputs (`see \\[home\\]`), so the branch introduces this. Fix: measure a fence's indent from the enclosing list item's content column rather than from column 0 (the same class as candidates 8 and 9), and add both inputs to TestEscapeBlockHazardsRich.

verdicts.tldr: No step of the calibration pipeline reads the new _Slow_ benchmarks, so the next re-fit pasted into native_gas.go silently drops the x2.45 and x2.95 hand factors
verdicts.details: gen_native_table.py:209-210 fits EscapeBlockHazards only from `BenchmarkNative_Markdown_EscapeBlockHazards_(\d+)-`. That pattern matches neither `_Slow_1000` nor any `EscapeBlockHazardsRich_*` name, and the script has no Rich row. The checked-in markdown_bench_output.txt has 0 Slow rows. A regenerated native_gas_table.go.txt would therefore carry the base-shape fit with no comment. The finder overstates one point: native_gas.go:184-185 does record the factors, in comments that read `27361×2.45 ... not re-fit` and `27597×2.95`. The loss is latent and needs a future re-fit and paste, so this is a Suggestion, not a Warning. The thread on the gas factors does not cover the pipeline wiring. Fix: add gen_native_table.py rows (regexes) for `EscapeBlockHazards_Slow_(\d+)` and `EscapeBlockHazardsRich_Slow_(\d+)` and fit the shipped slopes from them, or name the factors in the script's table so a re-fit keeps them.
verdicts.evidence: Read at a8bdd53b0: `grep -n 'EscapeBlockHazards\|Slow' gen_native_table.py` gives only lines 209-210 (`r"BenchmarkNative_Markdown_EscapeBlockHazards_(\d+)-\d+\s+..."`). `grep -c Slow markdown_bench_output.txt` gives 0. native_gas.go:184 `Slope: 67034 ... // 27361×2.45 (#6304 ... not re-fit ...)` and :185 `Slope: 81411 ... // 27597×2.95`. The bench run and re-fit were not run; the regex non-match is settled by the read.
